name: Title VII of the Civil Rights Act of 1964

slides.title: Introduction
slides.description:
• Purpose and Background
    1. Enacted on July 2, 1964
    2. Aim: To eliminate discrimination based on:
      • Race
      • Color
      • Religion
      • Sex
      • National origin in employment.
    3. Supreme Court up-date Ruling - June 15, 2020 added
      • Sexual Orientation
      • Gender Identity
  • Jurisdiction
    1. Applies to employers with 15 or more employees
    2. Covers all aspects of employment

slides.title: Prohibited Employment Practices
slides.description:
Prohibited employment practicesare actions by employers that violate laws designed to protect employees' rights and ensure fair treatment in the workplace. Key examples include:

  • Discrimination: Treating employees or job applicants unfairly based on race, color, religion, sex, national origin, age, disability, or genetic information. This includes hiring, firing, promotions, pay, job assignments, and other employment-related decisions.
  • Harassment: Allowing or engaging in behavior that creates a hostile or intimidating work environment, such as sexual harassment or bullying based on protected characteristics.
  • Retaliation: Punishing employees for exercising their rights under employment laws, such as reporting discrimination, participating in an investigation, or filing a complaintwith a government agency.
  • Failure to Accommodate: Not providing reasonable accommodations for employees with disabilities or religious practices, as required by laws such as the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) or Title VII of the Civil Rights Act.
  • Wage and Hour Violations: Not adhering to laws regarding minimum wage, overtime pay, or other compensation-related requirements.
  • Violating Employment Contracts: Breaching terms of an employment contract, which could include unjust dismissal or failure to provide promised benefits.
  • Health and Safety Violations: Ignoring regulations designed to ensure a safe and healthy work environment, such as those enforced by the Occupational Safety and Health Administration (OSHA).
  1. Discrimination Based on Race, Color, Religion, Sex, or National Origin
    1. Hiring and Firing
    2. Promotions and Transfers
    3. Compensation and Benefits
    4. Training and Development
  2. Sexual Harassment
    1. Quid Pro Quo Harassment
      • "Quid pro quo" is a Latin phrase that means "something for something" or "this for that." It describes a situation where one thing is given or done in exchange for another thing of roughly equal value. It's often used in legal or business contexts to indicate a mutual agreement or trade. For example, if someone provides a service, they expect to receive compensation in return. It can also have negative connotations if it implies an unethical or corrupt exchange.
    2. Hostile Work Environment
      • A "hostile work environment" refers to a workplace where an employee experiences harassment, discrimination, or other behaviors that create an intimidating, offensive, or abusive atmosphere. This can include:
        • Discriminatory Behavior: Harassment based on race, gender, sexual orientation, religion, disability, or other protected characteristics.
        • Unwelcome Conduct: Persistent, severe, or pervasive conduct that disrupts work performance or creates a hostile atmosphere.
        • Abusive Language: Verbal abuse, threats, or offensive comments.
        • Bullying: Intimidation, belittling, or aggressive behavior by colleagues or supervisors.
  3. Retaliation
    1. Retaliationin the workplace occurs when an employer takes adverse action against an employee for engaging in legally protected activities. This can include actions such as:
      • Reporting Discrimination or Harassment: If an employee complains about or reports discriminatory practices or harassment.
      • Whistleblowing: When an employee reports illegal or unethical behavior within the organization.
      • Exercising Legal Rights: Taking time off for medical reasons under the Family and Medical Leave Act (FMLA), or asserting other legal rights.
    2. Retaliatory actions might include:
      • Termination: Being fired or laid off after making a complaint.
      • Demotion: Losing a job title or position as a form of punishment.
      • Reduction in Hours or Pay: Experiencing a cut in salary or work hours.
      • Harassment: Facing increased scrutiny, bullying, or exclusion following a complaint.

questions.question: Title VII prohibits employment discrimination based on which protected categories?

answers.b: Race, color, religion, sex, and national origin

questions.question: Which update was included by the Supreme Court in June 2020?
What did the Civil Rights Act of 1991 add?

answers.a: Required yearly harassment training for all employees

questions.question: Which of the following best describes “retaliation”?

answers.b: Punishing an employee for reporting discrimination or participating in an investigation
Investigating complaints, mediating/settling disputes, and enforcing compliance
